items.name: HUD optical unit
items.desc: The finished optical unit on the dash: TFT PGU at the rear and lowest, the cold-mirror fold above it, the concave mirror at the front, the shutter and dust cover in the lid. Light leaves the crop, folds forward, is magnified by the concave mirror and leaves through the dust cover to the windshield, which reflects it to the driver.
items.where: dash top, in front of the driver, removable without tools

items.name: 3-D printed housing, baffles and lid
items.desc: The whole optical train lives in one printed, matte-black shell on the dash top. Panel and backlight sit at the rear, lowest, venting through the base; the fold sits above them; the concave mirror sits at the front; the dust cover and shutter close the top. It comes off without tools, so the car returns to stock.
facts: 12.5° (stays under the glass, over the fold)
printed matte black, layer lines inside break up reflections
four feet with soft pads; no tools, nothing bonded to the glass

items.name: Picture generation unit (TFT)
items.desc: The finished picture generator: the stock cell on the custom backlight, the half-wave retarder on top if the axis needs it, an NTC thermistor on the cell's back for the controller's derating, and the HDMI board on a bracket. Only the crop is lit and drawn; the rest of the panel is black.
facts: 10,000 cd/m² on axis; uniformity ±20% over the crop
946 × 473 px of 1920 × 1080 at 60 Hz over HDMI
thermistor derates, then blanks; 30 min at full power in a 40 °C box must stay under the rating
1.9 cd/m² at the eye by day, 0.05 at night (IPS 1,000:1, ASSUMED)
12.6 W LED, about 3.0 W absorbed in the cell

items.name: Custom direct-lit LED backlight
items.desc: The stock edge-lit backlight gives a few hundred cd/m². This replacement lights only the crop, from directly behind: eight high-power white LEDs on an aluminium board, a white mixing cavity, a diffuser plate, two crossed prism films and an infrared-cut glass, cooled by a finned heat sink and a 40 mm fan.
facts: 12.6 W at 50% efficiency, 150 lm/W (ASSUMED); 6.3 W with films
crossed pair, gain 2.0 (ASSUMED; 3M about 1.5 per film)
constant current, analogue + PWM dimming above 2 kHz (Recom RCD-24 class)

items.name: LCD cell, 60 × 30 mm crop lit
items.desc: The panel with its stock backlight removed. The cell makes no light: each subpixel is a voltage-controlled shutter between two crossed polarisers. Only a 60 × 30 mm crop in the middle is lit and drawn; the rest stays black.
facts: 87 px/deg, 1.51 mm per px at 7.5 m
6% (ASSUMED; Phase 5 measures stock luminance ÷ backlight luminance)
1,000:1 (ASSUMED IPS); black at night 0.05 cd/m² at the eye
about 3.0 W absorbed over 18 cm² at full backlight
linear; the axis is measured in Phase 5 (often 45° to the edges)

items.name: Half-wave retarder film
items.desc: The windshield reflects s-polarised light (perpendicular to the plane of incidence) 19 times better than p. The panel already emits linearly polarised light, but its axis may sit at 45° to the edges. A half-wave film rotates that axis to s at no cost in brightness.
facts: output angle = 2 × fast-axis angle − input angle
the measured panel axis is not already along s (Phase 5)
Edmund WP280 600 × 500 mm about £324; Knight Optical 305 mm £213

items.name: HDMI driver board and flex
items.desc: HDMI in from the Jetson, 1920 × 1080 at 60 Hz.
facts: 450 cd/m² (vendor); 87 cd/m² at the eye through the windshield path
HDMI in, MIPI DSI to the panel over a 40-pin FPC; 5 V on micro-USB

items.name: PGU bracket and cell thermistor
items.desc: Screws to the heat sink base. 10 kΩ NTC taped to the cell beside the crop, read by the controller.

items.name: Cold-mirror fold and IR absorber
items.desc: The flat fold between the panel and the concave mirror is a dielectric cold mirror: it reflects visible light and transmits infrared. Sunlight that the concave mirror focuses back into the housing loses its infrared half here, into a black absorber, before it can reach the cell.
facts: 48% of the focused solar power (ASSUMED): 42 W → 20 W
plane of incidence aligned with the windshield's; s-reflectance checked against the vendor curve

items.name: Concave relay mirror, 300 × 200 mm
items.desc: The one custom optic. With the panel 316 mm away, inside its 330 mm focal length, the mirror forms a magnified virtual image 7.5 m behind itself, which the windshield folds into the driver's view. Used 15.5° off axis, a plain sphere splits that image into two focal distances; a toroid with different radii in the two planes brings them together.
facts: tangential image 52.7 m, sagittal 4.1 m behind the mirror
Rt 685 mm, Rs 636 mm: both images at 7.5 m
320 × 165 mm at 1 m (traced here: about 331 mm wide)
42 W into a 6 mm spot (131 W/cm²) before filters

items.name: Sun shutter and servo
items.desc: Two thin black leaves cover the mirror aperture under the dust cover. A micro servo opens them through a Scotch-yoke lever; a constant-force spring pulls them shut, so the shutter fails closed if power or the controller stops. It closes whenever the HUD is off and whenever the sun-watch rule finds the sun in the entry patch.
facts: focused sun: 5.5 W in a 6 mm spot even after the filters (≈ 170 suns)
the HUD is off (parked car is the long-exposure case), sun-watch says so, cell too hot, or USB silent 5 s
21° × 11° of sky, 51° elevation behind the car; crossed in about 83 min
SG90-class micro servo on the HUD controller, 140 mm Scotch-yoke lever
constant-force spring closes it with no power

items.name: Dust cover, s-pass polariser, light sensor
items.desc: The window in the top of the housing. It keeps dust off the mirror, and a polariser laminated to its inside passes the HUD's own s-polarised light while absorbing more than half of any unpolarised sunlight trying to get in. The ambient-light sensor looks out through a window at one edge.
facts: s-pass (axis across the car); 42% of unpolarised light (ASSUMED)
s-polarised, so it passes almost unchanged
ambient-light sensor (TSL2591 or VEML7700) for the dimming curve
no polarised sunglasses: they block exactly this light

items.name: Stereolabs ZED 2i road camera
items.desc: The road camera and the HUD's main sensor. Its left lens is the origin of every coordinate in the plan. roadd reads its stereo pair for depth, fits the road plane each frame, lifts the lane and object detections onto it, and streams its IMU to egod.
facts: 4 mm: 80° × 52° (store page) vs 72° × 44° (datasheet), CONFLICT; f ≈ 1,144 px at 1080p from 80°
baseline 120 mm; depth 1.0/1.5–35 m; rolling shutter
1.64 m at 30 m for 0.25 px disparity (ASSUMED) → 0.047° at the eye
400 Hz; gyro gives egod a low-latency yaw rate
USB 3; ZED SDK 5.5.1 supports JetPack 6.2.x (installer needs an exact L4T match)
high on the windshield centreline, clamped to the mirror stalk; camera-to-eye 54 cm in this layout (plan ASSUMED 45 cm; keep within ≈ 0.5 m)
own RANSAC fit per frame (the SDK plane API needs tracking at ≈ 44% GPU)

items.name: Luxonis OAK-D Pro driver camera
items.desc: The driver camera. It finds the driver's face and eyes on its own processor and reports the eye midpoint, so hudd can re-project every graphic for where the eyes actually are; without it, a 150 mm head move shifts graphics by over a degree.
facts: global-shutter stereo pair (75 mm), RGB centre camera
IR flood + dot projector, for the head tracker at night
on-device depth and NN inference (RVC2): face detection and landmarks; BNO086 IMU
eye midpoint in the car frame + confidence, 30 Hz (eyePose); nominal eye after 500 ms stale
parallax for a 150 mm head shift: 1.15° at 7.5 m, 0.29° at 30 m
MediaPipe is unsupported on Jetson; on-camera landmarks are primary, OpenSeeFace the CPU alternative
$349–429 (range; plan line "Luxonis OAK-D Pro (driver camera)", last seen 2026-10-21)

velocity 0.05 m/s; heading 0.2°; dead reckoning ≈ 2% of distance
unbiased speed reference for age compensation; heading and time for the sun-watch rule
unspecified by u-blox (≈ 12 ms reported by one user): measured with the LED test
within 1 m/s of a reference GNSS trace while moving; dash without a fix

items.name: Seeed reComputer J4012 (Jetson Orin NX)
items.desc: The only computer in the car. It runs every HUD process: stereo depth and the ground plane, the lane and object networks, ego-motion, head tracking, the 60 Hz renderer and the logs. It drives the panel over its single HDMI port and streams the audience view over Ethernet.
facts: Jetson Orin NX 16 GB (8-core Arm, 1024-core Ampere GPU)
Seeed J401: 1x HDMI 2.1, no DisplayPort, 4x USB 3.2, GbE, CAN (unused)

items.name: HUD controller (RP2040) and sensors
items.desc: A Raspberry Pi Pico that owns the HUD's analogue world: it reads ambient light and the cell temperature, drives the backlight and the sun shutter, and enforces the thermal and watchdog rules on its own, so a stuck Jetson cannot cook the panel.

items.name: Mini-Box DCDC-USB-200 converter

items.name: Windshield (the combiner)
items.desc: The car's stock laminated windshield is the HUD's final reflector. Its inner surface reflects about a quarter of the s-polarised image toward the eye; the outer surface reflects a second, parallel copy offset by 3.1 mm. At a 7.5 m image that is 1.4 arcminutes, about two pixels, so the plan keeps the stock glass and draws thick lines and area fills.
facts: $600–1,500, only if the Stage 2 photo needs it
items.where: rake 28° (ASSUMED); the HUD reflects off its inner surface

items.name: Traced light path, panel to eye
items.desc: Rays traced back from the eye box through the corners and centre of the 10.8° × 5.4° window: eye ← windshield ← concave mirror ← fold ← panel. Light travels the other way.
facts: 310 mm (simulation; the plan's 250 mm does not clear the glass)

items.name: Eye box, 130 × 70 mm
items.desc: The region the driver's eyes can move in and still see the whole window, centred on the nominal eye point 1.22 m above the road.

items.name: Stage 0 bench rig
items.desc: The first optics are a desk rig for software: the panel lies face-up in a black enclosure under a 70/30 teleprompter beamsplitter at 45°. A camera or the developer's eye looks through the glass and sees the panel reflected, floating over whatever is behind. There is no virtual distance and no windshield; it tests the renderer, colours and latency, not the optics.
facts: 70/30 teleprompter glass at 45°; the first number is usually the transmitted share (verify with the vendor)
about 0.6 m from the camera (no magnification)
projection maths, colour and alpha, latency instrumentation
360 cd/m² from the 1,200-nit monitor (24% of the sky target)

items.name: Stage 1 Fresnel and combiner rig
items.desc: Before the custom mirror exists, a 300 mm Fresnel lens makes the virtual image: the panel sits 280 mm below it, inside its 300 mm focal length, like an object under a magnifying glass. A free-standing combiner glass above the dash folds the light to the driver. It tests registration at a 4.2 m image at night and in overcast light.
facts: Fresnel, 300 mm square, f = 300 mm; panel at u = 280 mm
v = 4.2 m on the panel side; M = 15
1.2 m × 0.6 m, 16° × 8°, 54 px/deg on the monitor
70/30 teleprompter glass above the dash (30% reflected)
360 cd/m² from the monitor: night and overcast only

items.name: Latency probe (photodiode + LED)
items.desc: Measures motion-to-photon latency end to end. The Pico flashes an LED in front of the road camera; perception sees it, hudd flips a test marker, and a photodiode on the panel catches the change. The time between is the latency the age compensation must cover.
facts: flash an LED at the road camera; time the panel change with a photodiode
whole chain ≤ 90 ms; estimate 37–99 ms uncompensated
a synthetic lanes step measures renderer + panel alone
the age hudd reports in hudStats
replay has no live latency: only this test measures the real chain
$300 (estimate; plan line "Latency probe, rangefinder, target board", last seen 2026-10-21)

items.name: Spot luminance meter on tripod

a calibrated camera, within about 20% above 5,000 cd/m²
$690–4,000 (range; plan line "Luminance meter (spot meter to lab meter)", last seen 2026-10-21)
